_about: Model providers a worker can run on. Prices are US dollars per million tokens. The launcher's default is deepseek, and its entry reproduces the harness's behaviour before providers existed. User overrides and opt-ins go in ~/.claude-deepseek/providers.json, never in a project.

meta.name: Meta Muse Spark
meta.unverified: Contributor is its own model name on the same key (dev.meta.ai/models/muse-spark, 2026-09-27); the max reasoning level is Standard-only. Effort support, rate limits, speed and availability in Australia: check with a key.

sol.name: OpenAI GPT-6.1 Sol (via OpenRouter)
sol.unverified: GPT-6.1 Sol (released 2026-09-29; model id gpt-6.1-sol, $2 / $10 per million, $0.10 cached, 1.05M context, prompts over 272K tokens cost 2x input and 1.5x output) through OpenRouter's Anthropic-format endpoint. OpenRouter says Claude Code is optimised for Anthropic models and other providers may not work correctly: tool calls, thinking, prompt caching and the effort setting are unproven here. OpenRouter charges a fee when credits are bought, which the recorded spend does not include. No balance check: OpenRouter has a credits endpoint that is not wired in.

xiaomi.name: Xiaomi MiMo
xiaomi.unverified: Token Plan: its allowance and how it counts usage are shown only in the console; spend records it at $0, so the dollar limits do not cover it.

allowance.source: mimo.mi.com/docs/en-US/price/token-plan (2026-09-27): monthly credits per plan; mimo-v2.6-pro credits per token (flash is cheaper, so counting at pro rates errs safe). Exhausted: service suspended until renewal.

xiaomi.role: Occasional background second opinions only, where speed does not matter (2026-09-27 comparison: review quality like DeepSeek but 1.5-4x slower; its content filter refused an ordinary engine review; images through Claude Code were slow and mixed up). DeepSeek stays the main worker.
